== The Wonderful Wizard of Oz ==

The Cowardly Lion, also known simply as the Lion or the Lion, is one of Dorothy's traveling companions on the road of yellow brick, joining her in the hope that Oz can give him courage he believes he lacks: "Do you think Oz could give me courage?" he asks, to which the Scarecrow answers that Oz could grant it "Just as easily as he could give me brains." Despite the name he carries, the Lion repeatedly proves capable and useful to the group: he measures a wide ditch and carries Dorothy, the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman across on his back one at a time, and later swims to shore towing the raft by his tail after the current sweeps the party away from the road. He hunts for his own food in secret rather than ask Dorothy to prepare cooked meat for him, and by his own admission is "really a wild beast."

The Wizard tells him that as long as the Wicked Witch of the West lives, he must remain a coward, a verdict that angers the Lion, though he says nothing in reply and rushes from the throne room when the Wizard's Ball of Fire grows too hot to face. Yet it is the Lion who scares away the Witch's slaves, one of the events that leaves her without the means to destroy Dorothy and her friends. After the Witch is melted, the Lion reports the news to a man they meet, stating gravely that it was Dorothy who melted her. When the Tin Woodman describes his new heart as kinder than his old one, the Lion declares in turn that he is afraid of nothing on earth and would gladly face an army or a dozen fierce Kalidahs. When the group must later choose whether to stay in the Emerald City or move on, the Lion decides to go with Dorothy, saying he is tired of the city and longs for the woods and country again.

=== Events ===

* A great Lion leaps out, knocks over the Scarecrow, and claws at the Tin Woodman without effect.
* Dorothy rushes forward and slaps the Lion's nose to protect Toto, calling him a coward.
* The Lion admits he is a coward, explaining his roar scares off every creature though he has no real courage.
* The Tin Woodman suggests the Lion's fear may be heart disease, noting he himself has no heart at all.
* The Lion asks to join the group so Oz might grant him courage, and Dorothy welcomes him.
* Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Lion camp overnight under a tree, with Dorothy sharing the last of her bread while the Scarecrow gathers nuts for her.
* They reach a wide, deep ditch, and the Lion agrees to jump over it carrying each companion across on his back one at a time.
* Deeper in the forest the Lion warns them about the Kalidahs, fierce beasts with bear bodies and tiger heads.
* The Lion swims to shore towing the raft by his tail, and Dorothy helps pole them to land.
* The poppies' scent overpowers Dorothy, Toto, and the Lion, putting them to sleep, while the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman remain unaffected.
* The Lion runs ahead but collapses asleep just short of the poppy field's edge.
* The Scarecrow and Tin Woodman carry the sleeping Dorothy out of the poppies to safety, forced to leave the Lion behind.
* The Scarecrow asks the Queen to help rescue the Cowardly Lion, who is asleep and trapped in the poppy field.
* The mice are harnessed to the truck and pull the sleeping Lion out of the poppy field to safety before Dorothy thanks them and they depart.
* Cowardly Lion wakes from poppy field, rescued by field mice, rejoins group.
* Landscape turns green; locals wear green, avoid group due to Lion.
* The Tin Woodman sees Oz as a monstrous five-limbed Beast, and the Lion sees Oz as a Ball of Fire; both are told the same condition for a heart and courage.
* The Witch sends her Winkie slaves with spears, but the Cowardly Lion's roar scares them off.
* The Witch uses her Golden Cap's third and final charm to summon the Winged Monkeys, who destroy the Scarecrow, batter the Tin Woodman, and capture the Lion.
* The Winged Monkeys spare Dorothy because of the Good Witch's kiss mark on her forehead and deliver her to the Witch's castle, where she is forced into servitude while secretly feeding the imprisoned Lion each night.
* Dorothy frees the Cowardly Lion from his prison after learning the Wicked Witch has melted.
* Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Lion get lost in the fields of buttercups and daisies while trying to walk back to the Emerald City.
* The Winged Monkeys carry Dorothy, Toto, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Lion through the air to the gates of the Emerald City.
* The Cowardly Lion goes to Oz to receive his promised courage.
* Oz gives the Lion a green liquid from a bottle and tells him to drink it as courage.
* The four companions meet in the Throne Room; the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and Lion each express contentment with what they gained from Oz, but Dorothy insists she wants to return to Aunt Em and Uncle Henry in Kansas.
* The Lion, Tin Woodman, and Scarecrow all agree to accompany Dorothy, and the group plans to depart the next morning.
* The group travels south in good spirits, with the Lion relieved to be out of the City and Toto chasing moths and butterflies.
* The Tin Woodman, Scarecrow, and Lion praise Oz, while Dorothy privately forgives him for not keeping his promise.
* The Tin Woodman builds a ladder while Dorothy, the Lion, and Toto rest after their long walk.
* The Lion accidentally smashes a china church with his tail while jumping onto the second wall.
* The Lion praises the forest while the Scarecrow finds it gloomy, and Dorothy worries about wild beasts.
* The tiger greets the Lion as King of Beasts and explains a giant spider-like monster has been killing the animals.
* The Lion agrees to fight the monster if the beasts will obey him as King of the Forest afterward.
* The Lion finds the sleeping monster, springs onto its back, and kills it with one blow, breaking its neck.
* The beasts bow to the Lion as King, and he promises to return and rule once Dorothy is safely on her way to Kansas.
* The Hammer-Heads used their stretching necks to headbutt the Scarecrow and the Lion, sending both tumbling down the hill.
* Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Lion tidy themselves before being brought before Glinda, who sits on a throne of rubies.
* Glinda uses the Golden Cap's three remaining commands to send the Winged Monkeys to carry the Scarecrow to the Emerald City, the Tin Woodman to the Winkies, and the Lion to his forest.
</div>

== Ozma of Oz / A Record of Her Adventures with Dorothy Gale of Kansas, the Yellow Hen, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tiktok, the Cowardly Lion, and the Hungry Tiger; Besides Other Good People too Numerous to Mention Faithfully Recorded Herein ==

The Cowardly Lion, also known simply as the Lion, rules the great forest as the King of Beasts. He knew nothing of Ozma until she became the reigning princess of Oz, after which he journeyed to the Emerald City to see her. On learning that she was about to visit the Land of Ev to set free its royal family, he begged to go with her and brought along his friend, the Hungry Tiger.

Despite his royal title, the Lion shows open unease when confronted with danger: faced with a great hammer swinging near his head, he shuddered and admitted it made him "dreadfully nervous."

=== Events ===

* Ozma leads an expedition of Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tiktok, Billina, the Cowardly Lion, and an army of Oz to free the Queen of Ev and her ten children from the Nome King.
</div>
